title: Gout: treating attacks and preventing recurrence
intro: Gout is inflammation caused by urate crystals in joints. Attacks can be extremely painful, often affecting a big toe, ankle or knee. It is not simply a consequence of eating badly or drinking alcohol.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: An attack usually causes rapid pain, warmth, redness and swelling. Other conditions, including joint infection, can look similar; a first hot swollen joint should not be diagnosed from appearance alone.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: Assessment includes the pattern, medicines and kidney health. Joint-fluid testing may identify crystals or infection. A urate level can be normal during an attack, so timing and follow-up interpretation matter. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Anti-inflammatory treatment for attacks is selected around kidney disease, ulcers and interactions. Long-term urate-lowering treatment is a different strategy, often requiring monitoring and initial flare prevention. Do not stop established urate-lowering medicine during a flare unless advised. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Rest the painful joint and try a wrapped cool pack if comfortable. Maintain hydration unless fluids are restricted, moderate alcohol and avoid crash diets. Diet changes support care but may not replace indicated medication. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Fever, severe illness or a new hot swollen joint needs urgent assessment for infection. Recurrent attacks, nodules or kidney problems warrant review of prevention and a clear treatment target.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira has a first red swollen knee and fever. She seeks urgent assessment rather than taking a relative’s gout tablets.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben feels well between attacks but continues agreed preventive treatment and monitoring because symptom-free days do not mean crystals have disappeared.
